WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"Let the work of this house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews build this house of God in his place." Ezra 6:7

He ordered the costs paid from "the tribute beyond the river", and sacrifices supplied, "that they may offer sacrifices of sweet savours unto the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king, and of his sons". Ezra 6:8–10

"And the God that hath caused his name to dwell there destroy all kings and people, that shall put to their hand to alter and to destroy this house of God which is at Jerusalem. I Darius have made a decree; let it be done with speed." Ezra 6:12
After the Passover Ezra says the LORD had "turned the heart of the king of Assyria unto them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God". Ezra 6:22
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
He supplied bullocks, rams, lambs, wheat, salt, wine and oil for the burnt offerings "day by day without fail". Ezra 6:9–10
He confirmed Cyrus's decree and paid the building costs from the tribute beyond the river. Ezra 6:6–8
He set a penalty on anyone who altered his word: timber pulled from his house and he hanged on it. Ezra 6:11
"And the elders of the Jews builded, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo." Ezra 6:14

SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Second, fourth and sixth years named; no length of reign.
LATE 522 – NOVEMBER 486 BC (PARKER AND DUBBERSTEIN, 1942)

On their tables his second year began on 3 April 520 BC, so Haggai's "sixth month, in the first day" (Hag 1:1) fell about 29 August 520; the twelfth month of his sixth year (Ezra 6:15) fell early in 515.
HERODOTUS: "KING IN ALL SIX-AND-THIRTY YEARS"
Herodotus gives 36 years; the end-points here are Parker and Dubberstein's.
Artaxerxes I, named for his later gifts to the house
C. F. Keil (1873), following Clericus and J. H. Michaelis

Keil holds that only Artaxerxes Longimanus can be meant, though he reigned long after the temple was finished, because his edict (Ezra 7:15, 21) later supported its upkeep. Ezra 6:14 Ezra 7:15 Ezra 7:21 [30]
Artaphernes, one of the seven Persian nobles who shared power with Darius
James Ussher (1658)
Ussher thought it "hard to understand any other than Artaphernes", taking the name as that of a partner in Darius's kingdom. Ezra 6:14 [25]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not tell how Darius came to the throne; his own inscription tells of the Magian Gaumata.
Scripture does not name Cambyses or the Magian who reigned between Cyrus and Darius, unless Ezra 4:6–7 refers to them (see the Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes pages).
Scripture does not say how long Darius reigned or that he ever saw Jerusalem.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textThis is the Darius of Ezra 4–6, Haggai and Zechariah, "Darius king of Persia". He is kept apart from Darius the Mede (Daniel) and from "Darius the Persian" (Neh 12:22), who have their own records. Ezra 4:24 Haggai 1:1 Zechariah 1:1 Daniel 5:31 Nehemiah 12:22
Scholars' viewScholars identify him with Darius I, son of Hystaspes, who reigned 522–486 BC.[10][3]
